title: The nftables in Istio's images is no longer pinned to 1.1.1 — nodes with an old nftables package can crash once a newer nft has run on them

detection.reason: the istio-cni ConfigMap's values and the nodes' package versions are not collected; the hint names the istio-cni DaemonSet and the command reads the nftables switch

quote: As a result, Istio is removing the `nftables` version pinning. Users are advised to update the `nftables` package on their nodes to the latest available version to ensure that the fixed version is installed. If you continue to experience `nftables` crashes on your nodes, downgrade to an older version of Istio and contact your node OS provider to request that the fix be backported to your OS version.
remediation: Only clusters that opted into native nftables (`global.nativeNftables=true`, rendered as `NATIVE_NFTABLES` in the istio-cni ConfigMap) are affected; iptables mode does not run nft. Before upgrading, update the `nftables` package on every node to a build carrying the upstream fix; a node whose nft crashes after the upgrade needs the fix from the OS vendor or a downgrade of Istio.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -n istio-system -l app=istio-cni -o json | jq -r '.items[].data.NATIVE_NFTABLES // "unset"'  # "true" means native nftables is on and every node's nftables package must carry the fix before 1.31

title: Gateway API CRDs below Istio's minimum bundle version are silently ignored (in effect since 1.30 for TLSRoute) — TLS passthrough gateways stop programming listeners

detection.reason: the bundle version is an annotation VALUE on the CRD and rules compare keys, not values; the hint names the four CRDs istiod version-gates and the command prints their bundle versions

quote: Resources backed by such CRDs are silently filtered by istiod, which previously made TLS passthrough breakage after upgrading to Istio 1.30 with stale Gateway API CRDs hard to discover.
remediation: istiod's CRD watcher drops any Gateway API CRD whose `gateway.networking.k8s.io/bundle-version` annotation is below its minimum: GRPCRoute needs bundle v1.1.0 and BackendTLSPolicy v1.4.0 (since 1.28), TLSRoute needs v1.5.0 since 1.30 and TCPRoute v1.6.0 since 1.31. A TLSRoute on a 1.4.x bundle is never read after upgrading to 1.30: the Gateway reports `attachedRoutes: 0`, no listener is programmed and passthrough traffic fails with no error in the resource status. Upgrade the Gateway API CRDs to at least the listed bundle before upgrading istiod; from 1.31 `istioctl analyze` reports it as IST0176.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd grpcroutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io backendtlspolicies.gateway.networking.k8s.io tlsroutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io tcproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -o custom-columns='CRD:.metadata.name,BUNDLE:.metadata.annotations.gateway\.networking\.k8s\.io/bundle-version' --ignore-not-found  # minimums: grpcroutes v1.1.0, backendtlspolicies v1.4.0, tlsroutes v1.5.0 (1.30), tcproutes v1.6.0 (1.31); a lower bundle is silently ignored

title: istiod now sends unhealthy endpoints to proxies unless a DestinationRule sets `outlierDetection.minHealthPercent`

detection.reason: applies to services WITHOUT minHealthPercent, an absence the projection cannot list; the istiod Deployment carrying the opt-out is the subject

quote: By default, Istio will now send unhealthy endpoints unless `OutlierDetection.minHealthPercent` is being configured on a Service. This can be disabled by setting `PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS` to `false` or using compatibility profiles.
remediation: For every service without `outlierDetection.minHealthPercent`, istiod now sends not-ready endpoints (marked unhealthy) and forces Envoy's panic threshold to 0 — the panic-mode fallback that used to spread requests over ALL endpoints when most were unready is gone, so such requests fail fast (`no healthy upstream`) instead. Set `outlierDetection.minHealthPercent` on the DestinationRules where panic mode was relied on, or set `PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS=false` on istiod.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release)/pilot"))) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("^(PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS|PILOT_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS)$")) | $n + ": " + .name + "=" + (.value // "(valueFrom)")'  # no printed line means unhealthy endpoints are sent after upgrade

title: Auto-registered WorkloadEntries created before 1.31 stay on plaintext until re-registered or labelled `networking.istio.io/tunnel=http`

detection.reason: the affected entries are auto-registered AND missing the tunnel label — two conditions on one object the vocabulary cannot combine; the auto-registered entries are the candidates

quote: workloads auto-registered before upgrading continue to be reached over plaintext until either they re-register (reconnect a fresh instance) or the label (`networking.istio.io/tunnel=http`) is added to their existing WorkloadEntry.
remediation: Only meshes where VM proxies speak HBONE are affected: ambient-enrolled VMs, or sidecar meshes running with `ENABLE_HBONE=true` on the proxy and `PILOT_ENABLE_SIDECAR_HBONE_LISTENING=true` on istiod. There, for each auto-registered WorkloadEntry (annotated `istio.io/autoRegistrationGroup`) without the `networking.istio.io/tunnel` label, restart the VM/proxy so it re-registers, or add the label by hand — until then that workload is reached over plaintext. A plain sidecar mesh's unlabelled entries are correct as they are.
verifyCommand: kubectl get workloadentries.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["istio.io/autoRegistrationGroup"] != null) | select(.metadata.labels["networking.istio.io/tunnel"] == null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # each printed WorkloadEntry was auto-registered before 1.31 and stays plaintext until it re-registers or is labelled

title: `PILOT_SPAWN_UPSTREAM_SPAN_FOR_GATEWAY` is removed — gateways always spawn an upstream span

detection.reason: checked on the istiod Deployment's container env NAMES only — a flag set through `pilot.env` in a values file lands there; one set via `meshConfig` or an IstioOperator that has not been applied yet is not scanned

quote: The environment variable `PILOT_SPAWN_UPSTREAM_SPAN_FOR_GATEWAY` has been removed. The behavior it controlled (spawning a separate tracing span for each upstream request for gateway when using the Telemetry API) is now always enabled.
remediation: Remove the variable from istiod. If it was `false`, gateway traces gain one extra span per upstream request at 1.31; adjust trace-volume budgets or sampling accordingly. `compatibilityVersion: 1.30` lists the flag but it is inert there too.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release)/pilot"))) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("^(PILOT_SPAWN_UPSTREAM_SPAN_FOR_GATEWAY)$")) | $n + ": " + .name + "=" + (.value // "(valueFrom)")'  # a printed line is the removed flag; a value of false means gateway traces gain an upstream span at 1.31

title: Large ambient meshes: ztunnel's reconnect request can exceed istiod's 4MiB gRPC limit and loop with `ResourceExhausted`

detection.reason: the trigger is the mesh's workload count, which the evaluator does not sum; the ztunnel DaemonSet marks an ambient mesh

quote: This request can exceed istiod's default 4MiB gRPC receive limit, leaving ztunnel in a reconnect loop with `ResourceExhausted: grpc: received message larger than max` errors.
remediation: On meshes near 40,000 workloads and services, raise `ISTIO_GPRC_MAXRECVMSGSIZE` on istiod before upgrading (about 1MiB per 10,000 resources, e.g. `--set pilot.env.ISTIO_GPRC_MAXRECVMSGSIZE=33554432`) and watch istiod logs for the error after upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods,workloadentries.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items | length | tostring + " pods+workloadentries"'  # near 40000 (plus services) raise ISTIO_GPRC_MAXRECVMSGSIZE on istiod before the 1.31 upgrade

title: istiod's XDS API generator now rejects MCP consumers from non-system namespaces

detection.reason: which workloads consume istiod's api generator is not on the cluster

quote: Custom MCP consumers connecting to istiod's api generator from non-system namespaces are now rejected. Standard sidecar, gateway, and ztunnel traffic is unaffected.
remediation: Move custom MCP/XDS-API consumers into the Istio root namespace (or give them a control-plane identity), or set `ENABLE_XDS_API_GENERATOR_AUTH=false` on istiod. Sidecars, gateways and ztunnel need nothing.
